subject.title: Feature: Native Audio Input for Omni-Modal Models (skip STT transcription)

question: Should OpenClaw add opt-in native audio model input for inbound channel audio, and what typed media, provider-egress, fallback, and transcript/audit contract should govern it?
rationale: The request is aligned with multimodal provider direction but changes core model content, provider routing, raw voice-byte egress, and session transcript semantics that cannot be safely inferred from current code alone.

options.title: Design contract first
options.body: Keep #51667 open as the canonical tracker, use #78797 as input, and require a maintainer-approved contract for typed audio blocks, provider capability routing, fallback, payload limits, and transcript/audit semantics before merge.

options.title: Accept candidate after review
options.body: Let #78797 become the implementation path only if it resolves compatibility, security-boundary, auth-provider, and real-behavior-proof blockers against the agreed contract.

options.title: Defer to plugin or provider layer
options.body: Decline core native audio forwarding for now and keep audio-only behavior in provider/plugin-specific media understanding until a missing core API is proven.

recommendation.title: Design contract first
recommendation.body: Keep #51667 open as the canonical tracker, use #78797 as input, and require a maintainer-approved contract for typed audio blocks, provider capability routing, fallback, payload limits, and transcript/audit semantics before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent provenance across the provider/model routing and core content paths this decision would change.
